title: pilosella bauhini subsp. magyarica
intro: Pilosella bauhini subsp. magyarica, commonly known as Hungarian fleabane, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the family Rosaceae. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The bioactive constituents of Pilosella bauhini subsp. magyarica include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as reducing inflammation, fighting oxidative stress, and exhibiting antimicrobial activity. The plant has been used to treat various conditions, including wounds, ulcers, and gastrointestinal disorders, and is also valued for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.
